beats.say: Simplify: on top, three to the power N plus one, minus three to the power N minus two,
asks: What is N here?

beats.say: all over three to the power N minus one, minus three to the power N plus two.
asks: Which part is the bottom?

beats.say: Every power is N plus or minus a number. The powers are different, so nothing cancels yet.
asks: Why can't I cancel the threes now?
Why are the powers different?

read: We can only cancel a factor: something that multiplies the WHOLE top and the WHOLE bottom.
The top is $3^{n+1} - 3^{n-2}$, two terms taken away.
$3^{n+1}$ is only one of those terms, so it cannot cancel on its own.
So first make $3^n$ multiply every term: split each power.
Then take $3^n$ out of the top and out of the bottom.
**Cancel only what multiplies the whole top and the whole bottom.**

beats.say: The plan: make every term show three to the power N. Then take it out, top and bottom, and cancel it.
asks: Why three to the power N?
What do the box and triangle mean?

beats.say: Split the power: three to the power N plus one is three to the power N times three to the power one.
asks: Why can I split the power?
Is it times or plus?

beats.say: This is Add power in reverse: multiplying adds the powers, N plus one, back to the question.
asks: Which law is this?
How do I check a split?

beats.say: In the same way, three to the power N minus two is three to the power N times three to the power negative two.
asks: Where does negative two come from?

beats.say: Below, three to the power N minus one is three to the power N times three to the power negative one.
asks: Why is it negative one?

beats.say: And three to the power N plus two is three to the power N times three squared.
asks: Why is it three squared?

beats.say: A split is always a times. A common mistake is writing three to the power N plus three.
asks: Why is it not plus three?

beats.say: Now every term has three to the power N, so take it out of the top and out of the bottom.
asks: How do I take it out?
Is this factorising?

beats.say: Each bracket keeps what is left of its terms: the powers one and negative two on top, negative one and two below.
asks: What goes inside the brackets?

beats.say: Three to the power N multiplies the whole top and the whole bottom. Divide both by it, so it cancels.
asks: Why can I cancel it now?

beats.say: Only numbers are left. A negative power is one over: three to the power negative two is one over nine.
asks: Why is a negative power one over?
Can I use the calculator now?

beats.say: And three to the power negative one is one third. Three squared is nine.
asks: Where does the nine below come from?

beats.say: Now the calculator: the top is twenty-six over nine, the bottom is negative twenty-six over three.
asks: How is the top twenty-six over nine?
Why is the bottom negative?

beats.say: Dividing by a fraction is times its flip, so the twenty-sixes cancel. The answer is negative one third.
asks: How do I divide the two fractions?
